records.source_title: TOMRA: Annual Report 2025 - Tomra Systems ASA (Cision)
records.excerpt: TOMRA has approximately 119,900 installations in over 100 markets worldwide. The Group had total revenues of EUR 1,318 million in 2025 and employs 5,800 people globally.
records.population: TOMRA Group
records.does_not_establish: Group totals say nothing about how much revenue, if any, comes from individual consumers rather than business and government customers.

records.source_title: TOMRA Annual Report 2025: Circular Foundations
records.excerpt: Our solutions serve retailers, waste managers, recyclers and governments to enable recycling of a wide range of materials, and they serve farmers, packhouses and food processors to optimize the food production value chain.
records.population: TOMRA customer groups across divisions
records.does_not_establish: It names customer groups but gives no revenue split by group and does not say whether any farmers are small or private buyers.

records.source_title: TOMRA Annual Report 2025: Circular Foundations
records.excerpt: Our main activities include the development, production, and sale or lease of reverse vending machines, as well as servicing these. In some markets, TOMRA processes the material after its collection, and provides data and clearinghouse solutions for the DRS. In 2025, 39% of revenues stemmed from equipment sales while 61% stemmed from the different services offered.
records.population: TOMRA Collection (reverse vending) customers
records.does_not_establish: It shows the revenue mix of the reverse vending business but not who pays for each service or any consumer-paid revenue.

records.source_title: TOMRA Annual Report 2025: Circular Foundations
records.excerpt: TOMRA’s solutions are divided into six product lines – Basic, Mini, Standalone, Flexible, Revolution and Expert – which can be tailored to local market needs. These cater for all store sizes – from small kiosks to large hypermarkets and professional counting and redemption centers.
records.population: Retail stores and redemption centers hosting reverse vending machines
records.does_not_establish: It does not show how many small kiosks actually buy or lease the machines, or at what price.

records.source_title: TOMRA Annual Report 2025: Circular Foundations
records.excerpt: Reverse vending machines automate the take-back process of beverage containers and provide regulatory compliance for retailers. They also drive consumer footfall to the stores where most collection points are found and where the refunded deposit will typically be spent.
records.population: Retailers hosting reverse vending machines and their shoppers
records.does_not_establish: It states the retailer benefit TOMRA claims but does not measure footfall or show how retailers would view a direct consumer offer.

records.source_title: TOMRA Annual Report 2025: Circular Foundations
records.excerpt: We assessed potential impacts related to consumers and end users where applicable at TOMRA as the majority of the people handling our products are not consumers or end users.
records.population: People handling TOMRA products, as assessed in TOMRA's sustainability statement
records.does_not_establish: The statement comes from a sustainability materiality assessment, mainly about safety impacts, and does not measure consumer demand or consumer revenue.

records.source_title: myTOMRA App - App Store (Australia)
records.excerpt: myTOMRA makes recycling more fun and convenient than ever before. Collect your recyclables, return them to your nearest recycling point and collect your digital refunds.
records.population: Users of TOMRA reverse vending machines with the myTOMRA app
records.does_not_establish: The free app handles deposit refunds; it does not show that consumers pay TOMRA for anything.

records.source_title: myTOMRA deposit return system app reaches 10 million user sessions
records.excerpt: Reached a new milestone of 10 million user sessions and the equivalent of 50 million euros paid in deposit refunds
records.population: myTOMRA app users
records.does_not_establish: Sessions and refunds paid out are usage of a free refund service, not purchases from TOMRA, and the figures are from 2022.

records.source_title: myTOMRA deposit return system app reaches 10 million user sessions
records.excerpt: With no retailer obligation in the New South Wales’ DRS, TOMRA saw value in a consumer app that could instead offer digital payout of refunds, and a map to show recyclers where to return their containers.
records.population: Recyclers in the Return and Earn deposit scheme
records.does_not_establish: It explains why the app was built for one scheme design and does not show the app works or pays off where retailers host return points.

records.source_title: TOMRA acquires collection solution provider C&C Consolidated Holdings
records.excerpt: Bag drop is a convenient collection method whereby consumers can drop off entire bags of empty beverage containers at collection points and have their deposit refunded. It is a well-established and popular complement to reverse vending machines and redemption centers in North America, with strong growth potential.
records.population: Consumers returning deposit containers through CLYNK bag drop
records.does_not_establish: It does not give CLYNK's revenue, how many consumers use it, or whether consumers or retailers pay for the service.

records.source_title: TOMRA Annual Report 2025: Circular Foundations
records.excerpt: Based on our first pilot with Aarhus municipality in Denmark, and subsequent pilots at sports events and festivals, we continue to develop the solution to become sufficiently convenient for both consumers and for the cafés and restaurants serving takeaway food and drinks.
records.geography: Denmark and other European pilot sites
records.population: Consumers and cafés using TOMRA Reuse takeaway packaging
records.does_not_establish: It shows TOMRA Reuse is still being developed through pilots; it does not show consumer uptake, willingness to pay or who pays.

records.source_title: Fruit sorting, grading, packing, and filling solutions - TOMRA Food
records.excerpt: Single and Dual Lane Sorters are ideal for small-to-medium packhouses but also connectable to our larger Multi Lane Sorter. They can pack into a wide variety of packaging types.
records.population: Small-to-medium fruit and vegetable packhouses
records.does_not_establish: It does not give prices or show that individual farms, as opposed to packhouses, buy these sorters.

records.source_title: myTOMRA App - App Store (Australia), ratings and reviews
records.excerpt: I have been using Tomra system for a number of years and have had to up with the machinery malfunctioning sometimes breaking down forcing me to relocate to another Tomra site.
records.population: One myTOMRA app user
records.does_not_establish: A single review shows one user's frustration with machine downtime; it is not representative of all users.

records.source_title: Re-turn replaces some Deposit Return Scheme machines - RTÉ News
records.excerpt: However, it added, a number of retailers decided to switch RVMs to an alternative manufacturer. The statement comes as some consumers have complained machines were not working when they tried to return bottles and cans and collect their deposits.
records.population: Retailers and consumers in Ireland's deposit return scheme
records.does_not_establish: The article does not name which manufacturers' machines failed or were replaced, so it does not show these complaints concern TOMRA machines.

records.source_title: Shop Where You Drop: A Survey of Consumer Bottle Return Habits - NYPIRG
records.excerpt: Survey results showed that the majority of respondents shopped frequently at the same location where they were returning beverage containers. Respondents also overwhelmingly chose to visit that specific retail location partially or mainly due to the convenience of the bottle return system offered by the retailer.
records.population: 1,107 people redeeming containers at 96 retail locations in 2011
records.does_not_establish: It shows that returns are tied to shopping trips at stores, not that consumers would pay for a home or personal return product; the data are from 2011.

records.source_title: One Billion Beverage Containers: How Return-It Express is Changing Recycling - Return-It
records.excerpt: While each independently owned and operated depot has the option to offer the Express service, it’s been shown that depots offering the service to their customers are seeing more beverage containers returned at their depots. With over 400,000 registered customers and growing, Return-It is committed to seeing the program becoming more accessible to all corners of the province.
records.population: Registered users of Return-It Express bag drop
records.does_not_establish: Return-It is a not-for-profit stewardship body offering a free account service, so its uptake does not show consumers would pay a company like TOMRA.

records.source_title: Smart Composters Are Heading to Retail, But Will Consumers Bite? - The Spoon
records.excerpt: None of these are cheap, especially for a fairly new product category like smart composters, which is probably why Lomi felt the need to start sending demo teams into markets in California and Washington to show people what these products are all about.
records.population: Buyers of home food-waste appliances
records.does_not_establish: It is a commentary on a different product category (home composting) and gives no sales or return-rate figures.

records.source_title: Tomra - Wikipedia
records.excerpt: Via several acquisitions, TOMRA had secured 75% global market share in RVMs, 60% in material recovery and 40–65% in sorting.
records.population: Reverse vending, material recovery and sorting markets
records.does_not_establish: The share figures sit in the article's 2010–2019 history section and are not current; they say nothing about consumer products.

records.source_title: Get rewarded to recycle while saving the earth! Swedish startup raises €4.1 million to show how - Tech.eu
records.excerpt: The free-to-use app’s 300,000 users in the Nordic region recycle more than 1.4 million packages every month. According to the platform, it has helped save over 1,000 tonnes (1 million kg) of CO2.
records.population: Users of the Bower recycling rewards app
records.does_not_establish: The user figures come from the company via the press, and a free app's users do not show willingness to pay.

records.source_title: Optical sorting grades potatoes by size and quality - FreshPlaza
records.excerpt: As many as 73 per cent of users have eliminated manual re-sorting. The modular system can be expanded with additional outlets or cameras. Farmsort.one, developed within the Grimme Group, is in use on more than 50 farms.
records.population: Farms using the Farmsort.one potato sorter
records.does_not_establish: The figures come from the vendor's press material, give no price, and concern farm businesses rather than individual consumers.

records.source_title: Deposit Return Scheme: drinks producer and retailer responsibilities - GOV.UK
records.excerpt: Supermarkets, grocery stores, convenience stores and newsagents that sell drinks in the scheme must host a return point for drinks containers, unless they qualify for an exemption. The return point can be manual or automated using a reverse vending machine.
records.population: Retailers selling drinks in the deposit scheme from 1 October 2027
records.does_not_establish: The rule obliges retailers to host return points; it creates no obligation or demand for consumers to buy return equipment.

records.source_title: PPWR - Reloop Platform
records.excerpt: Member States are required to set up a deposit return system for beverage cans and plastic bottles in order to reach a 90% collection for recycling target by 2029. Exemptions may be issued to a Member State that has achieved 80% collection by 2026.
records.population: EU Member States
records.does_not_establish: This is an advocacy group's summary of the regulation, not the legal text, and it says nothing about consumer-facing products.
